A battered hull surface fills one edge of the frame — riveted grey panels streaked with scoring, a row of grab-rails, a cluster of antennae and a glowing inspection-light, the astronaut's gloved hand braced on a handhold.

A vast gold-foil solar-array wing stretches diagonally across the foreground, its segmented cells catching brilliant sunlight, a thin truss spine and bundled cabling running its length toward an unseen ship.
The dark looming hull of a derelict ship dominates one side, hull-plates peeled and twisted, a shattered porthole, dead antennae, the astronaut tiny against its silent scarred flank.
A girdered docking truss crosses the foreground, heavy clamps and coiled umbilical lines, a tether running from the astronaut's waist to an anchor-point, a winking status-beacon.

A tumbling communications satellite drifts close, its large dish canted at an angle, folded solar panels half-extended, loose cabling spiraling outward, the astronaut reaching toward a recessed service panel.

A massive comms dish the size of a building curves across the frame, its latticed mesh surface pocked with microimpact craters, a central feed-horn assembly bristling with smaller antennae and sensor spurs.

An open airlock hatch dominates the near edge, thick pressure-door seals framing a warm amber interior glow, safety-striped jambs, a retractable ladder rail, and a status-panel scrolling green telemetry.
A drifting cargo container fills the foreground, hazard-striped yellow and black panels bolted over a heavy aluminum frame, stenciled serial numbers, a broken magnetic clamp trailing frayed wiring.
A damaged engine nozzle looms close, its bell-mouth scorched deep black and cracked along one flank, ablative tiles missing in jagged patches, a warped heat-shield bracket hanging loose on one bolt.

The ribbed spine of a starship stretches from corner to corner, a long dorsal keel of interlocked titanium frames, conduit runs and cabling lashed to cleats, the structure vanishing in atmospheric haze far below.

A habitat module curves through the near field, its cylindrical skin studded with lit portholes glowing warm amber, insulation blankets secured by velcro strips, a junction box bristling with coax connectors.

A tether line snakes diagonally across the foreground, braided steel cable catching sunlight, a spring-loaded anchor clamp fixed to a hull stanchion, the far end disappearing off-frame into blackness.
A pressurized equipment rack floats loose nearby, its open face exposing circuit boards, bundled fiber runs, and slide-out avionics trays, one drawer half-ejected, a warning light pulsing amber.

A fuel-line manifold clusters in the foreground, thick high-pressure hoses joined by hexagonal couplings, frost crystals blooming where a slow propellant leak vents silently into vacuum, valves marked in faded red.

A collapsed radiator panel hangs at an angle from fractured hinges, its corrugated white surface discolored by thermal cycling, embedded heat-pipe fins visible at the broken edge, loose mylar flapping.

A sensor boom extends into frame, a slender carbon-fiber rod studded with magnetometers and particle detectors, each instrument wrapped in gold and silver foil, a junction box at its root trailing ribbon cable.

A modular science platform brackets the astronaut's position, its aluminum struts bolted to a main truss node, experiment canisters slotted into numbered bays, a camera head tracking slowly on a motorized pivot.
A grapple fixture and berthing ring occupy the near edge, a heavy hexagonal collar of brushed steel with alignment pins and latching hooks, a data-port panel and proximity sensor cluster flanking it.

A meteoroid-shield panel lies peeled back from the hull, its multi-layer Whipple construction exposed in cross-section — foil, mesh, foam, and backing plate — edges curled outward from a dime-sized penetration hole.

A power-distribution node clusters in the near field, a thick junction housing trailing eight separate conduit runs in different colors, circuit-breaker handles, a voltmeter display, and cable ties every few centimeters.
A crumpled antenna array folds across the foreground, three thin dipole elements bent at wrong angles after a collision, a cracked base-plate still bolted to the hull, a coax feedline dangling free.

A thermal-control louver assembly covers a large hull section, rows of angled aluminum slats adjusting in real time, actuator rods visible between them, a temperature sensor strip running the full width.

A robotic arm cradle fixture anchors the scene, its massive shoulder socket empty, locking pins extended, hydraulic umbilical ports open, an interface panel showing a frozen fault-code display in dim red digits.

A pressurized tunnel adapter bridges two modules in the near field, a short cylindrical collar of flanged rings and bolt patterns, its interior hatch open and glowing, handrails running the inner circumference.

A defunct relay satellite tumbles slowly into frame, its rectangular bus chassis bare of insulation, two broken solar paddles spinning independently, a cracked transponder housing trailing a ribbon of shredded Kapton foil.
